limitations: Training OOF rows fit the calibrator; their fit is not independent calibration evaluation.
The candidate was selected using the same grouped CV, creating selection reuse bias.
2023 validation has prior exploratory exposure and is not an independent final test.
The global sigmoid targets an unweighted censored row mixture, not event-balanced or operational prevalence.
OOF scores come from smaller fold models, possibly with different class weights; transfer to the final full-train model is an unverified assumption.
Positive sigmoid slope preserves ordering/period monotonicity mathematically; fixed logit clipping and floating point ties may change AP numerically.
Positive metric reductions mean improvement on these same exposed validation rows; no deploy decision or response threshold is selected.
